Markwayne Mullin Is in Hot Seat After String of Glitches (and a Football Game)
 
Plus, what’s driving the Democrats’ Senate leadership fight, and Trump’s pick to lead the Navy faces a choppy confirmation hearing
 
 
ELIZABETH FRANTZ/REUTERS
 

Good morning. Markwayne Mullin has been talking a lot these days. It isn’t always going well. And he’s headed back to Capitol Hill on Wednesday.

 

On Friday, the homeland security secretary was at the White House when he tried to explain to reporters why thousands of flights were suddenly grounded.

 

“My understanding is that we can still communicate, it’s just at different levels and the clarity we can get to, but there’s redundancy in most communications so as you can see, there’s still planes landing,” Mullin said.

 

The next day, while thousands of U.S. travelers were still dealing with the havoc wreaked by Friday’s disruption, Mullin flew to Texas for a prime-time college-football game. According to the New York Post, he met in a luxury box with a DHS contractor.

 

Asked about this on CNBC Tuesday morning, Mullin deflected the question and said Rep. Steve Scalise (R., La.) had arranged the ticket.

 

Mullin is testifying with Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton on Wednesday about threats facing the U.S. Clayton was a late add to the schedule, and could take pressure off Mullin from having to explain everything. Since Mullin is a former senator, it would normally be a friendly audience. But then again, it might not be.

 

In the past week, there have been plenty of glitchy things happening in the U.S., enough to have people scratching their heads and wondering a) what is going on? and b) who is in charge? There are conspiracy theories flying all over social media about what is causing these glitches. President Trump and top members of his cabinet are in Asia.

 

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the root cause of the flight problem is still being investigated. The vibe from the administration went from “nothing to see here” to “we’re looking into it” over the span of a couple of hours.

 

Mullin will likely get grilled on it all Wednesday. The White House hasn’t given his agency a ton of independence, and DHS secretaries don’t tend to last too long in Trump’s orbit. He’ll have a chance to address all these concerns in front of Congress.

 

This is an edition of the Politics newsletter, bringing you an expert guide to what’s driving D.C. every day. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

People and Policies I’m Watching

 

House Democrats: Lawmakers will hold leadership elections to nominate a House speaker candidate and select a majority leader, whip, conference chair and other junior positions.

 

JD Vance: The vice president will speak at the New York Times DealBook summit in New York.

 

Trump’s Wednesday: The president wrapped up his visit to the Philippines and is in Shenzhen, China.

What I’m Following

 
 
SIOBHAN HUGHES/WSJ
 

Progressive grassroots anger is driving the Democrats’ Senate leadership fight. Activists are demanding new leadership after the midterm elections and backing Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland for a majority leader. Meanwhile, supporters of Sen. Chuck Schumer’s candidacy see the New York Democrat as the deserving architect of the midterm wins, even if some take issue with his leadership style.

 

Democrat Mary Peltola unseated Alaska GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan. With 99% of the vote counted, Peltola—the first Alaska Native elected to the U.S. Senate—had 50.1% to Sullivan’s 45.8%, according to the Associated Press. Her victory will bring Democrats’ Senate majority to 56 seats when they take control of Congress next year.

 

Trump’s pick to lead the Navy faced a rocky reception from Republicans and Democrats during his confirmation hearing. Hung Cao revealed that the U.S. Navy has been using expired Tomahawk missiles in the Middle East due to the military’s shortage of critical munitions. He also parried with lawmakers on the living conditions and mental health of the sailors serving extended deployments. Here are takeaways from the hearing.

 
 
 

What Else Is Happening

 

• The Trump administration pulled the nomination of Dr. Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration.

 

• Trump’s pick to lead the Government Accountability Office drew objections from Senate Republicans.

 

• Kalshi will no longer list some betting markets associated with Trump.

 

• The Federal Aviation Administration halted installations of routers after last week’s nationwide ground stop.

 

• The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia after the resignation of Chief Executive Jensen Huang.
